label: Poincare's Last Geometric Theorem
notes: Open by framing this appendix as Poincare's parting gift to dynamics. He could not prove the statement he needed for the restricted three body problem, so he published it as a conjecture in nineteen twelve. Stress that one fixed point of a map can mean a whole periodic orbit of a flow.

label: The Annulus and Its Boundaries
notes: Establish the stage carefully. The closed annulus has two boundary circles, an inner one and an outer one, and a radial coordinate interpolating between them. Every later picture lives here, so make sure students see the annulus as the natural arena where a return map of a two degree of freedom system acts.

label: The Twist Condition
notes: Explain that a twist map advances angle by an amount that varies with radius. The decisive hypothesis is opposite rotation on the two boundaries, so the angular displacement changes sign across the annulus. Draw the shearing of a radial fiber on the board and have students predict where displacement must vanish.

label: Statement of the Theorem
notes: State the Poincare Birkhoff theorem precisely. An area preserving homeomorphism of the closed annulus satisfying the boundary twist has at least two fixed points. Emphasise the count two, not one, since the parity argument forces a second point once a first exists. Contrast conjecture with Birkhoff's nineteen thirteen proof.

label: Why Area Preservation
notes: Drive home that area preservation is not decoration. Without it one can rotate the inner and outer circles oppositely yet sweep all interior points around with no fixed point at all. Show the counterexample sketch and let students feel that measure conservation is what pins the orbits in place.

label: From Flows to Maps
notes: Connect the abstract map to mechanics. Choosing a surface of section in an energy level reduces a continuous Hamiltonian flow to a discrete return map. Liouville's theorem makes that map area preserving in suitable coordinates, so the topological hypotheses of the theorem are met by genuine mechanical systems.

label: Periodic Orbits as Fixed Points
notes: Make the dictionary explicit. A fixed point of the return map is a trajectory that closes after one circuit, so it is a periodic orbit of the flow. A point of period q for the map is an orbit closing after q crossings. This is why fixed point theorems become existence theorems for periodic motion.

label: The Birkhoff Argument
notes: Sketch Birkhoff's reasoning without full rigour. The set of points whose angle is unchanged forms a curve joining the two boundaries because the twist forces a sign change. Area preservation then prevents that curve from being pushed entirely inward or outward, forcing intersections that are the fixed points.

label: The Restricted Three-Body Problem
notes: Return to Poincare's motivation. In the restricted three body problem he sought periodic solutions near a known one and reduced the search to fixed points of an area preserving annulus map. The geometric theorem was exactly the missing lemma guaranteeing those periodic orbits exist.

label: Infinitely Many Periodic Orbits
notes: Show the harvest. Applying the theorem to iterates of the map, and to rational rotation numbers between the two boundary rotation values, yields fixed points for every such ratio. Each gives a periodic orbit, so a single twisting area preserving map carries infinitely many distinct periodic orbits.

label: Worked Twist Map
notes: Walk through the explicit standard twist example. The map advances angle by a radius dependent amount and leaves radius fixed before a perturbation. Verify the Jacobian has determinant one and that the boundary rotations have opposite sign, so the hypotheses hold and two fixed points are guaranteed.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Close by collecting the three pillars: the annulus arena, the twist hypothesis, and area preservation. Remind students that the theorem launched modern symplectic topology and the Conley Zehnder and Arnold conjectures. Leave them with the slogan that conserved area turns a twist into guaranteed periodic motion.
